findings.title: The added Fātiḥa frame makes help devotional and directional
findings.claim: Through the explicitly added Fātiḥa frame, the focus's named Allah and sought-help predicate can also be heard inside a communal act of exclusive worship and a request for guidance when testimony is contested.
findings.mechanism: Fātiḥa 1:5 places worship and seeking help in one direct-address pair, while 1:6-1:7 specify guidance along a straight path away from error; these external triggers return through the focus Allah and help words and add a discernment-oriented devotional frame.
findings.reader_payoff: The final appeal gains a concrete practice of asking for help to stay oriented while reports and surfaces compete.
findings.containment: This is an external overlay only. It does not make worship or guidance lexical meanings of 12:18, and it does not replace the native reading of Jacob's appeal against the brothers' description.

epistemic.reason: The external Arabic and word coordinates are supplied, but the selected context unit carries no explicit source-trust label; the overlay is therefore kept qualified.
